signature.name: Warsaw Old Town
signature.detail: The reconstructed heart of the city, rebuilt brick by brick after WWII and now a UNESCO site. It is the essential first stop for any visitor. Go early in the morning to enjoy the squares before the crowds arrive.

signature.name: Palace of Culture and Science
signature.detail: A towering Soviet-era landmark that dominates the skyline and houses museums, theatres and a viewing terrace. Head up to the terrace for panoramic views, ideally around sunset. Buy tickets on arrival.

signature.name: Royal Castle, Warsaw
signature.detail: The former residence of Polish kings on Castle Square, richly restored with grand interiors. It anchors the Old Town and is a must for history lovers. Book tickets ahead in peak season to skip the queue.

signature.name: Łazienki Palace
signature.detail: An elegant palace on an island in the middle of a beautiful park, surrounded by gardens and peacocks. It is a peaceful escape from the busy centre. Visit on a weekday morning for quieter paths.

signature.name: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews
signature.detail: A striking modern museum telling a thousand years of Jewish history in Poland. It is one of the city's most acclaimed cultural sights. Allow at least half a day and check opening days before you go.

signature.name: Warsaw Uprising Museum
signature.detail: A powerful, immersive museum devoted to the 1944 uprising, with moving exhibits and artefacts. It is essential for understanding the city's modern identity. Book timed tickets in advance.

signature.name: Wilanów Palace
signature.detail: A baroque royal palace with formal gardens on the city's southern edge. It makes a rewarding half-day trip away from the centre. Take a bus or taxi and go early to beat the crowds.

food: Casual meal $8-15; pierogi and milk-bar lunches under $10
transport: Tram or metro about $1 a ride; taxis moderate
